      The structures are the ones on the Neuroanatomy Lectures Worksheet, plus the pons. Most shapes are real anatomy from one adult brain segmented with FreeSurfer, plus small nuclei from the CIT168 atlas fitted to that brain. Structures no atlas here labels are carved from that brain's tissue or modelled from its landmarks, so treat these as approximate: fornix, septum pellucidum, anterior commissure, lamina terminalis, pineal gland, cerebral aqueduct, interventricular foramen, olfactory and optic pathways, anterior perforated substance, tectum, cerebral peduncles, pyramids, dorsal columns, pons, internal capsule, corona radiata, uncus, Wernicke's area and the longitudinal fissure. Distances run between structure centres in millimetres. Paired structures count once.
